## Course Overview

This course introduces the mechanical behavior of structural elements subjected to common engineering loads. The focus lies on stress analysis, deformation, and stability of structural members.

The material forms the foundation for later courses in structural engineering, mechanical design, and aerospace structures.

## Learning Objectives

After completing the course, students should be able to:

- compute stresses and strains in structural members
- analyze torsion in circular and thin-walled shafts
- determine stresses in beams subjected to bending
- compute beam deflections
- evaluate the stability of columns and predict buckling loads

## Course Topics

### 1 Axially Loaded Members

- normal stress and strain
- Hooke's law
- deformation of bars
- statically indeterminate problems
- thermal stresses
- stress concentrations

### 2 Torsion

- torsion of circular shafts
- shear stress distribution
- angle of twist
- statically indeterminate torsion
- thin-walled sections

### 3 Beam Bending

- internal forces in beams
- normal stresses due to bending
- shear stresses in beams
- section properties
- beam deflection
- statically indeterminate beams
- thin-walled beams

### 4 Buckling

- stability of columns
- Euler buckling theory
- effective length
- critical load

## Assessment

Assessment may include:

- homework assignments
- written examinations
- optional project work
